newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares edge up in lower volume.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares edge up in lower volume.

text.p: 0940 GMT - Istanbul shares firmed slightly in weaker volume on Wednesday morning as range-trade began ahead of a forthcoming parliamentary vote of confidence in the newly formed right-left coalition government, brokers said.
* The IMKB National-100 ended the session seven points, or 0.38 percent, firmer at 1,858 after moving in a tight range between 1,878 and 1,849.
* Morning volume dropped further to 10.59 trillion lira from Tuesday's 12.49 trillion.
"There was light profit taking after shares opened higher. Selective activity in shares affecting the market index continued," said Erden Gokay from Taksim securities.

"I expect the index to remain within 1,800 and 1,900 range until the confidence vote on July 12. Afterwards, the market direction will depend on government decisions to be taken on economic issues," he added.
The new government headed by conservative Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz will read in parliament its programme on Monday. It will face a confidence vote on July 12.

* Of the 246 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 102 to 54 and 90 were steady. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.52 percent to 1,740, the IMKB Services gained 0.49 percent to 1,863 and the IMKB Financial rose 0.74 percent to 2,029.
Actives were led by largely state-owned flat steel maker EreglI, utility Cukurova Elektrik and state oil refiner Tupras, steady at 24,500 lira, 255,000 lira and 86,000 lira, respectively.
